metadata.name: game_content
metadata.description: Centralized game content data and admin-configurable tables

instructions.name: activate_tag_rulebook
docs: Atomically publishes the next sealed rulebook version for new operations.

instructions.name: add_admin
docs: Root admin grants delegated admin access to another wallet.

instructions.name: append_tag_rules
docs: Appends a bounded transaction-sized batch while the rulebook is unsealed.

instructions.name: bootstrap_missing_class_configs
docs: Idempotently provision any missing built-in class accounts and repair the
empty action arrays produced by older class-creation flows.
Existing valid class content is never reset: customized stats, names,
actions, tags, and enabled state are preserved exactly.

instructions.name: bump_equipment_content_revision
docs: Invalidates cached equipment after mutable item content changes.
This instruction is also the CPI boundary used by the Items program
when an individual item's authored tags are replaced.

instructions.name: close_enemy
docs: Close an Enemy instance account; rent refunded to `recipient`.

instructions.name: close_enemy_type_config
docs: Close an EnemyTypeConfig; rent refunded to `authority`.

instructions.name: close_environment_config
docs: Close an EnvironmentConfig; rent refunded to `authority`.

instructions.name: close_item_type_config
docs: Close an ItemTypeConfig; rent refunded to `authority`.

instructions.name: create_class_config
docs: Create a new player class configuration

instructions.name: create_enemy
docs: Create a battle-ready enemy account (admin only)

instructions.name: create_enemy_type_config
docs: Create a new enemy type configuration

instructions.name: create_environment_config
docs: Create a new environment configuration

instructions.name: create_item_type_config
docs: Create a new item type configuration

accounts.name: tag_registry
docs: Equipment-content revision invalidated by every canonical type change.

instructions.name: create_tag_rulebook
docs: Starts authoring exactly the next rulebook version in the active lineage.

instructions.name: initialize_registry
docs: Initialize the game content registry (one-time setup by admin)

instructions.name: initialize_tag_registry
docs: Creates the permanent root registry for custom tags and immutable rulebooks.

instructions.name: register_tag_definition
docs: Allocates the next stable custom tag ID and binds it to canonical metadata.

instructions.name: remove_admin
docs: Root admin revokes delegated admin access.

instructions.name: seal_tag_rulebook
docs: Permanently seals a rulebook and records its canonical digest.

instructions.name: set_class_action
docs: Set a default action for a class at a specific slot

instructions.name: set_class_action_tags
docs: Replaces authored traits on one configured class action.

instructions.name: set_class_tags
docs: Replaces traits snapshotted into players subsequently created from this class.

instructions.name: set_enemy_tags
docs: Replaces the authored traits on a concrete enemy instance.

instructions.name: set_enemy_type_tags
docs: Replaces the authored traits inherited by this enemy-type configuration.

instructions.name: set_environment_tags
docs: Replaces authored traits on an environment configuration.

instructions.name: set_item_type_granted_action_tags
docs: Replaces authored traits on the action granted by this item type.

instructions.name: set_item_type_tags
docs: Replaces authored traits supplied by this canonical item-type definition.
Item consumers compose these with the concrete instance's authored tags.

instructions.name: transfer_authority
docs: Transfer registry authority to a new admin

instructions.name: transfer_tag_authority
docs: Transfers tag-authoring authority without changing any existing tag meaning.

instructions.name: update_class_config
docs: Update class configuration

instructions.name: update_enemy_type_config
docs: Update an existing enemy type configuration

instructions.name: update_environment_config
docs: Update environment configuration

instructions.name: update_item_type_config
docs: Update item type configuration

types.name: TagClauseV1
docs: One canonical fixed-capacity predicate clause.
The active prefix is nonzero, sorted, and unique. Unused slots must remain
zero-filled, preserving one deterministic wire representation per clause.

types.name: TagDefinition
docs: Human-readable metadata for a tag, addressed by `id` in its PDA seeds.

types.name: TagEffect
docs: A fixed-width rule result. Basis-point channels use 10_000 = 100%.

types.name: TagEffectChannel
docs: Orthogonal numeric channels produced by tag rules.

types.name: TagNameIndex
docs: Permanent uniqueness index for a canonical custom tag name.
Definitions are addressed by numeric ID for efficient tooling, while this
PDA prevents two IDs from ever acquiring the same human-readable meaning.

types.name: TagPredicateV1
docs: Allocation-free role predicate.
`required_all` must all be present. At least one `required_any` tag must be
present unless that clause is empty. No `forbidden_any` tag may be present.

types.name: TagRegistry
docs: Root singleton for authority, custom-ID allocation, and rulebook activation.

fields.name: equipment_content_revision
docs: Monotonic invalidation epoch for cached equipment state. Any mutation
to a concrete item's authored tags or canonical ItemTypeConfig bumps it.

types.name: TagRuleV1
docs: A bounded predicate for each role in the tag context.

types.name: TagRulebook
docs: A preallocated rulebook that becomes immutable once sealed.
Rules may be appended over multiple transactions until `seal` computes the
canonical digest and locks the account. Publishing a replacement creates a
new version whose `previous_rulebook` points to the formerly active account.

types.name: TagSetV1
docs: A fixed-capacity set stored as a strict ascending prefix and zero padding.
Deserialization cannot enforce semantic invariants, so account/argument
boundaries must call [`TagSetV1::validate`] (or a higher-level API that does).

types.name: TagStage
docs: Runtime boundary at which a tag rule may be evaluated.
